guarantees.claim: When AES192Enable is true, rnd_type[0] is asserted if and only if rnd equals 0.
When AES192Enable is true, rnd_type[1] is asserted if and only if rnd equals 1, 4, 7, or 10.
When AES192Enable is true, rnd_type[2] is asserted if and only if rnd equals 2, 5, 8, or 11.
When AES192Enable is true, rnd_type[3] is asserted if and only if rnd equals 3, 6, 9, or 12.
When AES192Enable is false, rnd_type is forced to zero regardless of rnd.
When AES192Enable is true and rnd is not in {0,1,4,7,10,2,5,8,11,3,6,9,12}, all bits of rnd_type are zero because all equality comparisons evaluate false.

assumptions.claim: The AES192Enable parameter must be set to 1 only when the AES key length is 192 bits.
assumptions.cond: when AES key expansion is active
assumptions.risk: If violated, rnd_type may be forced to all‑zeros (if AES192Enable=0) or produce a 192‑bit mapping (if AES192Enable=1) in a mode that expects a different schedule, leading to incorrect expanded key and potential key corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The intended behaviour when rnd > 12 is unclear. The RTL outputs all‑zero rnd_type, which is distinct from the rnd=0 case, but it is not documented whether this is a safe fallback or a missing error detection.
uncertain_points.cond: when AES192Enable is true and rnd takes a value outside 0‑12
uncertain_points.risk: If such a value appears due to a counter glitch or logic error, the key expansion may silently use an incorrect round constant, corrupting the expanded key without any alert.
